W1 (mechanism), after E025.

**Tip: E023**
- Same math as E017, cut to 9.0 true epochs: 25 steps/epoch, 225 steps at batch 2000.
- Muon on the conv filters. The filters are renormalized every step, and muon_update applies no weight decay at all, so filter wd is literally absent. Newton-Schulz runs 3 steps.
- SGD on BN biases, whitening bias and head, wd 0.006.
- Lookahead every 5 steps with alpha exponent 3. Resolution 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps. CUDA graphs.
- Score: 6.198 s, 0.7538.
- Correction from my misses: new ideas are applied to the current tip. E024 and E025 ran on E023, not E017, which is why my time forecasts for them missed.

**Noise**
- Rebuilding the same commit: about ±0.04 pp.
- Any change to RNG consumption or code path reshuffles the 3-seed mean by about ±0.3 pp.
- True tip mean: about 0.7535–0.754 at 9.0 epochs. The margin over 0.753 is about 0.1 pp, so any change of 0.3 pp or less is a coin flip at 3 seeds.

**Time model (train is GPU-bound and follows pixel-steps)**
- Steps: E020 and E023 time scaled about 1:1 with step count. Fixed overhead (prepare, whitening, transfer) is about 0.25 s.
- Resolution: the 26 px middle phase (E024) cut about 4% of pixels and gave −2% time.
- Width cuts return about 50% of their MAC savings (E021).
- Per-step overhead (Muon NS on small matrices, Lookahead, fused SGD) is a few percent of a step at most. So changing batch size at fixed epochs saves little time.
- Rough FLOP count: about 0.9 GFLOP forward per 32 px image, about 900 TFLOP per run in roughly 5.9 s of train. That implies a high achieved rate (over 100 TFLOP/s), so kernel-efficiency levers are probably small.
- Group 1 (whitening plus the 31×31/15×15 convs) is about 20% of conv MACs, plus a larger share of memory-bound BN/GELU work.

**Accuracy exchange rates (pp lost per 10% of time saved)**
- Epochs: about 0.25 (E020, E023).
- Width: about 0.3–0.45 (E010, E021).
- Resolution: about 1 or more (E011, E018, E024). Even 28→26 px cost about 0.28 pp for 2% of time. Low-resolution phases are expensive to cut; the 3×3 final-map regime did not save E024.
- The epoch dial is the cheapest lever.

**Measured mechanisms**
- Lookahead/EMA: +1 pp (E005).
- Muon plus batch 2000: +0.5 ± 0.3 pp (E006).
- Resizing: −20% time for −0.5 pp (E007).
- Flat within noise: label smoothing 0.2, Muon lr ×1.5, LR floor 0, wd ×0.5 / ×0.25.
- Alpha exponent 2 (E025): +0.19 pp at 3 seeds, at the edge of noise. It may be a small real booster (about 0.1 pp). The held-out result is unknown to me.
- The regime is insensitive to optimizer and regularization scale. No 0.3 pp booster has been found.

**Strategy**
- Spend roughly 0.1 pp per step through micro-trims: −0.25 epoch gives about −2.7% time.
- Combine with a free averaging gain (alpha exponent 2) if held-out seeds confirm it.
- Mechanism-level savings that do not lose accuracy: backward truncation (FreezeOut) and fewer effective samples (selection). Both are risky. Selection changes the data distribution under heavy label smoothing. FreezeOut forces group-1 LR to 0 early, but group 1 matters less late in training.

**Unsure**
- Held-out means of E023 and E025.
- Per-layer TFLOP/s.
- Whether larger batches under Muon really avoid the per-step accuracy penalty. My prior is that they don't at this short horizon.
- PCIe transfer to the judge.

forecasts.reason: Diagnostic with no recipe change, so the scores reproduce the tip. A rough FLOP count (~900 TFLOP in ~5.9 s) implies 32 px convs above 90 TFLOP/s.
Branch (b): 225→219 steps gives −2.7% time 1:1 and about −0.07 pp, buried in the ±0.3 pp RNG reshuffle.
Skips about 15% of a 32 px step over a ~1.95 s tail, saving ~0.27 s (~4.5%, at the bar). Early LR-to-0 for group 1 costs ~0.1–0.25 pp.
−9% steps, but dropping easy samples under LS 0.3 skews the data, and changing reduction to mean risks rescaling the SGD-group gradients. Expect no better than the epoch-dial rate.
Same pixels, so only per-step overhead is saved (~1–2%). 20% fewer optimizer steps on a short horizon costs ~0.2–0.3 pp.
Optimizer-scale knobs have been flat (E014 ×1.5 gave +0.09). With renormalized filters, ×2 lr only changes the rotation rate, so a 0.2 pp held-out gain is unlikely.

cruxes: What are the held-out (seeds 3–12) means of E023 and E025? If alpha exponent 2 is a real gain of 0.15 pp or more, it funds a −0.5 epoch trim (to about 5.9 s).
What TFLOP/s do the 32 px vs 24 px steps achieve per layer? If above 100, systems levers are exhausted and only step-count and backward-truncation cuts remain.

Does truncating group-1 backward in the 32 px tail (I043) really save about 15% of tail step time without more than 0.2 pp held-out loss? That is the only untried mechanism that cuts compute without cutting data passes.
